title: Hypersurge sequence-aware token prober for streaming completions (SSE/WebSocket)
creator: Marina Ortiz
description: Implement a horizontal, sequence-aware load harness that emulates realistic streaming chat/completion traffic across SSE and WebSocket protocols. The harness must synthesize correlated token bursts, prefix/KV-cache warm/cold states, multi-tenant mixes, and variable response lengths to surface p95 token-latency and tokens/sec regressions. Outputs feed into our regression detector which compares rolling baselines and triggers alerts when performance deviates beyond configurable thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Supports SSE and WebSocket clients with multiplexed sessions and per-session variable prompt lengths
Can synthesize controlled KV-cache warmup patterns and report cache-hit vs miss p95s
Measures tokens/sec (global and per-tenant), latency histograms (p50/p95/p99) and token-stream completion jitter
Integrates with regression detector pipeline and emits Datadog and Grafana metrics/dashboards
Automated CI job that runs nightly baseline comparison and fails if regression threshold exceeded
PRs merged with unit/integration tests and a runbook for diagnosing alerts
metrics_targets: Aggregate tokens/sec target for staging harness: 2,000,000 (sustained 5m window)
P95 end-to-end token latency < 200ms for small (<=128 tokens) responses on canary hardware
Regression sensitivity: detect >=3% change in p95 with >90% confidence over 1 hour
False positive rate for regression alerts < 1% across 30 days of synthetic runs

notes: Trade-offs: prioritizing signal fidelity over absolute max QPS. Goal is realistic p95 regressions not synthetic peak QPS trophies.
We chose a hybrid driver (Node + Go) because Node simulates browser-like SSE better while Go sustains long-lived WS multiplexing with lower GC noise.
Instrumentation must expose per-segment KV cache hit rate to correlate with latency shifts — otherwise regressions are noisy and hard to triage.
